open_points.subject: A5 rule 1 Authorization parsing and validation
open_points.question: Does `deliverer_router` own checking header cardinality, the case-insensitive Bearer scheme and the required single space while extracting the presented token, despite being forbidden to own checks other than request-form checks; or does `deliverer_api` own those checks even though it is assigned only comparison of the token?
options: `deliverer_router` validates the field count and Bearer syntax and extracts the token; `deliverer_api` only compares it
`deliverer_router` only retrieves raw header values; `deliverer_api` validates all Authorization syntax and compares the token
Introduce a separate authentication module that validates and compares the Authorization field
open_points.default_guess: Treat Authorization-field cardinality and Bearer parsing as routing-boundary validation owned by `deliverer_router`, and leave only constant-time token comparison to `deliverer_api`.

witness.initial: A request has two `Authorization` fields and also has a malformed project id and body.
events: The caller sends the request to a token-protected route.
The router applies the authentication and request-form responsibilities described by State 3.
outcomes: The router treats field cardinality and Bearer syntax as part of reading the single field, rejects before parsing identifiers or the body, and never calls token comparison.

The router obeys its prohibition on non-request-form checks and delegates Authorization validation elsewhere; its own request-model processing can reject the malformed project id or body unless an unstated interface guarantees that the delegated check runs first.
witness.observer: The caller sees `unauthorized` in the first implementation and may see `invalid_request` in the second; module tests also observe different owners and call order.
